identity.note: arXiv 2611.03806 v1 (2026-11-02, Bjerregaard ... Krogh, Boomsma, Winther, Marin) names the leaderboard and GitHub repo in its comment. The GitHub repo MachineLearningLifeScience/BEND2 (org repo, not a fork, created 2026-11-02) links the paper, leaderboard, PyPI bend2 and HF dataset yhsure/BEND2 as 'BEND 2.0 data release'. PyPI project_urls list the same repo and HF dataset. The HF dataset carries the arxiv:2611.03806 tag, and the repo's only contributor login (yhsure) matches the HF account. The HF dataset is a personal account, but author-endorsed, not a third-party re-upload. Not a duplicate of bfm-bend (BEND, ICLR 2024, frederikkemarin/BEND): different paper, repo, package, tasks (design and edit effects versus gene finding and chromatin) and leaderboard. Same acronym family with overlapping authors (Marin, Krogh, Boomsma, Winther). Separate record is defensible. The curator may still prefer a version link or cross-reference in bfm-bend.

scope.note: This is a benchmark: code, data and a leaderboard for evaluating genomic and DNA language models, with no model weights of its own. It is broader than one task (8 tasks on 5 experimental datasets, per the abstract and README). A paper is not the only artifact: it ships a reusable package, data and a leaderboard.

identity.note: arXiv 2507.07860 (v1 2025-07-10, v3 2026-02-17; Marza, Fillioux, ... Vakalopoulou) names https://github.com/MICS-Lab/thunder as its code. The repo (not a fork, created 2025-05-15, pushed 2026-11-02) carries the same title; its README tells users to pip install thunder-bench, and PyPI thunder-bench 0.2.2 has summary 'THUNDER: Tile-level Histopathology image UNDERstanding benchmark'. The leaderboard is the repo's GitHub Pages homepage. No baseline match on name, aliases, arXiv ID or MICS-Lab URLs. The nearest neighbours (PathBench, HEST-1k, SpaPath-Bench) are different resources. NeurIPS 2025 D&B spotlight: arXiv comment and README, and an OpenReview API search lists note b2rzUJbLmS with venue 'NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track spotlight'. The proceedings page was not checked.

scope.note: Benchmark with leaderboards for pathology foundation models: 23 models on 16 datasets in the paper. Axes: downstream tasks (kNN, linear probe, segmentation, few-shot, zero-shot VLM), feature-space analysis, robustness, and calibration/uncertainty (ECE, MCE, SCE, ACE, TACE in calibration_metrics.py). It accepts user-defined models and custom datasets. The modality 'benchmark' is correct; PathBench and HEST-1k set the precedent. Uncertainty is measured on probes over frozen embeddings, not as a native model output.

artifact.note: Code is public. GitHub releases v0.1.0 (2025-07-10) to v0.2.2 (2026-01-27). PyPI thunder-bench 0.2.2. The leaderboards page resolves and lists UNI, Virchow, H-optimus, CONCH, Phikon, Midnight and a SPIDER leaderboard. THUNDER has no model weights of its own. Datasets are not redistributed: per-dataset loaders download them from upstream hosts (Zenodo, Warwick, UFPR, Hugging Face), and MHIST needs a manual data-access form. The current package covers 21 datasets (the paper's 16 plus SPIDER and others added later).

terms.note: CORRECTION NEEDED. Code is CC BY 4.0 per the repo LICENSE, the GitHub licence API and PyPI license_expression; that is a content licence, not a software licence. Both proposals left dataset terms unreviewed and set noncommercial=false. Upstream checks show the benchmark suite includes datasets with NC terms: BACH Zenodo 3632035 cc-by-nc-nd-4.0; ESCA Zenodo 7548828, SegPath Zenodo 7412731 and TCGA-uniform Zenodo 5889558 'other-nc'; histai/SPIDER-breast and SPIDER-colorectal cc-by-nc-4.0 with gated=auto on HF. In addition, MHIST needs a data-access form, Path2AI/STARC-9 has no hub licence, and the OCELOT Zenodo record shows no licence field. These datasets are core to the benchmark's runs and leaderboards. Under the 'ANY artifact or access route' rule, and the UKBBGym/JUMP-lite/HEST-1k precedent, noncommercial must be true. Benchmarked encoders also carry their own gated or NC terms; that alone does not set the flag (HEST-1k precedent).

identity.note: The 2021 bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2021.11.09.467890; v1 2021-11-11, v2 2022-01-19, CC BY, no journal version per bioRxiv API) and the repo J-SNACKKB/FLIP are the same official artifact. FLIP is not in the baseline: no FLIP, FLIP2 or flip.protein.properties hit in fm_identity.tsv (615 lines). It appears only as an input dataset in the held bfm-protein-uq note. MATERIAL OMISSION: the proposal describes FLIP only as it stood in 2021. The same official repo merged a 'FLIPv2 release' (commit 2026-03-03, PR #27 merged 2026-04-23). A FLIP2 preprint is posted (bioRxiv DOI 10.64898/2026.02.23.707496, 2026-02-24, CC BY 4.0, Didi ... Dallago, Yang), and its project site https://flip.protein.properties links 'Code' to J-SNACKKB/FLIP and Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18433203. The site also keeps the legacy FLIP datasets 'for continuity and comparison'. FLIP2 is the current version of the same lineage, by an overlapping author group, so the record should cover it and should not be split into a second record.

scope.note: This is a dataset benchmark: curated train/test splits plus baselines used to evaluate protein sequence representations, including pLMs (FLIP2 baselines include zero-shot pLMs and fine-tuned models). It belongs in the same family as the displayed TAPE, PEER and ProteinGym records, and 'benchmark' is the correct modality. It is not a single-task predictor. The Protein UQ scope objection does not apply: Protein UQ was held as a method-comparison study with a hard-coded representation, while FLIP is the reusable dataset/split resource itself.

artifact.note: Confirmed: the repo splits/ folder lists aav, bind, cas, conservation, gb1, meltome, sav, scl, secondary_structure; the data server http://data.bioembeddings.com/public/FLIP/ returns an Apache directory index (aav, bind, cas, conservation, fasta, gb1, meltome, sav, ...); Zenodo record 18433203 (version v3, 2026-01-30, cc-by-4.0) holds split files for legacy sets plus the new FLIP2 sets (e.g. amylase, hydro); the FLIP2 site serves per-split downloads (amylase, ired, nucb, trpb, hydro, rhomax, pdz3 plus legacy). No model weights are claimed or needed. The proposal missed the Zenodo deposit and the FLIP2 sets.

terms.note: Code: AFL-3.0 (GitHub licence API, LICENSE file). Data: the Zenodo record is CC BY 4.0. The FLIP2 site says the data are licensed 'under CC-BY 4.0 or MIT. See individual README files for details'. Per-dataset READMEs carry upstream terms; for example, the meltome README quotes the originators: 'Free for anyone to use. No need for licenses.' The bioembeddings raw-data server states no licence. Both preprints are CC BY 4.0. No NC terms were found on any route, so noncommercial=false is correct. However, upstream terms were sampled for meltome only, not for every dataset. The proposal's status ('Splits, notebooks and baselines under Academic Free License 3.0') wrongly implies the split data are AFL-3.0; the data terms are CC BY 4.0 / MIT per README.

urls.note: All three proposed URLs resolve: the DOI returns 302 to bioRxiv and ends at 200, GitHub returns 200, and the data server returns 200 with a directory listing. Labels are accurate. The FLIP2 DOI, project site and Zenodo DOI should be added; all were fetched (DOIs 302 then 200, site 200).

text.note: The description calls all split sets 'fitness landscapes', but scl (subcellular localisation), secondary_structure, conservation, bind and sav are residue- or protein-level property tasks added in the repo, not fitness landscapes. The io statement should say 'fitness and other protein property labels'. Year is 2021 for FLIP and 2026 for FLIP2. 'A common component of later benchmarks' was not evidenced by the proposer, so it is reworded to what was fetched. The README says FLIP was 'submitted to the 2021 NeurIPS Benchmark track' and the FLIP2 site claims ICML 2026 (Spotlight); neither proceedings listing was checked, so neither venue goes in the record.

identity.note: arXiv 2610.24002 (von Querfurth ... Bunne, submitted 15 Oct 2026, comment 'Accepted to NeurIPS 2026') names spora, spora [io] and spora [bench]. Both repos are under github.com/bunnelab (Bunne lab, EPFL; not forks), link back to arXiv 2610.24002 and the portal, and carry the same NeurIPS 2026 E&D-track BibTeX. The portal (spora.bioimagearchive.org, which redirects to /projects/spora) carries the same citation and links the repos and docs. No 'spora' name, alias or URL in baseline/fm_identity.tsv. Related but distinct baseline records: bfm-virtues (bunnelab/virtues) and bfm-kronos/bfm-kronos2 are models that spora [bench] evaluates, not duplicates. NeurIPS acceptance is self-reported in the arXiv comment and repo BibTeX; no proceedings page was checked.

scope.note: This is a dataset plus benchmark resource, not a model, so it routes to modality 'benchmark' (MAINTENANCE.md: datasets/leaderboards -> benchmark), which matches baseline precedents such as HEST-1k and PathBench. It is reusable and covers several tasks (6 pipelines: in-cohort cell probing, cross-cohort segmentation, cross-cohort cell annotation, tissue-level pathology, MPX-to-MPX and H&E-to-MPX virtual staining), and it explicitly targets SP foundation models (VirTues, KRONOS). Scope passes. The spatial lane may also propose it; keep a single record.

artifact.note: Data artifact confirmed beyond the landing page. The public S3 bucket bioimaging-01-pub at livingobjects.ebi.ac.uk (the endpoint used in the portal's rclone command) returns an anonymous ListBucketResult for spora-submissions/allam2022spatially/, showing a LICENSE file and .ome.zarr image chunks dated 2026-08-11. The portal's dataset browser lists 35 cohorts (BIA-SPORA-### accessions). Exception: the lin2022multiplexed prefix exists but listed no files and has no LICENSE (404), so that cohort may not be uploaded yet. Code in spora-bench (configs, models, spora_bench) and spora-io (pyproject, spora_io, scripts). No GitHub releases in either repo. spora releases no model weights of its own; bench model configs point to the third-party VirTues and KRONOS repos and checkpoints.

terms.note: Correction needed. (a) The spora-io LICENSE file is the MIT License (EPFL copyright header). GitHub reports NOASSERTION only because the header was modified; the README says 'released under the MIT Licence' and the docs footer says 'spora-io MIT'. The proposal's 'spora-io licence not confirmed' is wrong. (b) spora-bench is confirmed as CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 in both the LICENSE file and the README. (c) Data terms vary by cohort; the docs say 'Dataset licences vary'. I read each cohort's LICENSE file in the bucket: 30 are CC BY 4.0; 3 are CC0 1.0 (greenwald2026temporal, haist2026lymph, hickey2023organization); 1 is CC BY-NC 4.0 (klein2026explainable); 1 has no LICENSE file (lin2022multiplexed, 404). The spora-io README notes its MIT licence does not cover the datasets. (d) Access has no gating and needs no sign-in (anonymous S3/rclone). noncommercial=true is correct because the bench code is NC-ND and one cohort is CC BY-NC.

urls.note: All 4 proposed URLs return HTTP 200 and show what their labels say. arxiv.org/abs/2610.24002 shows the paper. github.com/bunnelab/spora-bench shows the benchmark code. github.com/bunnelab/spora-io shows the data interface. spora.bioimagearchive.org redirects to spora.bioimagearchive.org/projects/spora, the official portal hosted on the BioImage Archive (EMBL-EBI), and is not an aggregator. One addition: the official docs at spora.epfl.ch/docs/ (the repos' homepage field) state the code and data licences.

text.note: The description, io, use cases and year (2026) match the abstract, READMEs and portal (13,546 MX images, 5,477 patients, 35 cohorts, five technologies). Two small fixes. (2) The segmentation and annotation pipelines evaluate segmentation and annotation methods (e.g. MAPS, astir), not FM representations, so the io and description wording is broadened a little. name: RFD4-Proteina (RFD4-Proteína)
reason: Found by the rename/version sweep of the RFdiffusion and Proteina families: a joint Baker Lab (IPD) x NVIDIA GenAIR model released 2026-10-19/21, absent from the baseline under any normalised name or alias. All four gates verified: a 116-page preprint on the official project site (v1 and v2, 2026-10-21), the official repository (BSD-3-Clause), the official hub bundle with weights and SHA256 files, and exact per-artifact terms. Identity flag for the curator: the name sits between two existing records - bfm-rfdiffusion already carries the aliases RFdiffusion3/RFD3, and bfm-proteina is the NVIDIA Proteina record - so this could be filed as an alias of bfm-rfdiffusion instead of a new record. I propose a separate record because it is a new jointly developed model with its own repository, weights, preprint and licence, not a version bump of either parent.

scope.note: In scope. Primary abstract (PDF p.1, read locally): a shared chemical and conformational latent space over 'standard and modified amino acids, sugars, DNA, and RNA', with recurrent refinement and constraint-guided search, and 'The same model performs equivalently to or better than state-of-the-art specialist methods for side-chain packing, sequence design, conformational sampling, and design refinement' - i.e. one pretrained checkpoint across many tasks, not a single-task predictor. Reusable pretrained artifact confirmed (pretrained base in base/, release bundle at the root, PyPI/container/Diffusers load routes). Modality 'protein' is defensible and follows the bfm-rfdiffusion precedent (RFD3 is filed as protein although it handles ligands and nucleic acids); the curator could argue for 'complex' since bfm-proteina-complexa sits there and RFD4 designs protein-DNA, protein-ligand and glycan complexes. I leave modality as proposed and flag it as the curator's call; not a scope failure either way. No structural-model exception is needed: this is a generative design model, not a single-task structure predictor.

terms.note: Licences are exactly confirmable, but two of the proposal's terms statements do not survive checking. (a) Code and weights: BSD 3-Clause confirmed twice - GitHub licence API reports BSD-3-Clause with path LICENSE, and the hub LICENSE file is the BSD 3-Clause text, Copyright (c) 2026, Institute for Protein Design, University of Washington; the hub card states 'The BSD 3-Clause license covers the RFD4-Proteína model, weights and code only.' (b) DATA WORDING OVERSTATED: the proposal and the proposed status say 'training data CC BY 4.0'. The dataset card says CC BY 4.0 covers only 'the added annotations, sampling tables and indices', while 'upstream terms apply to the structures' (PDB CC0 1.0; AlphaFold DB, GlycoShape, CATH CC BY 4.0; PLINDER, TED, OMol25, CPSea, RNAcentral, MGnify credited per component README). (c) NONCOMMERCIAL FLAG DISPUTED: the proposal sets noncommercial=false while itself recording that the official hub repository distributes alphafold2/runtime/ and openfold3/runtime/ container images whose upstream terms, in the authors' own words, 'restrict commercial use or redistribution'. Under the run's rule (noncommercial=true if ANY artifact or access route has NC terms) and the catalog's own precedent for NC material redistributed inside an official artifact (bfm-runs-n-poses is noncommercial=true solely because the repo bundles AlphaFold 3 example outputs under the AF3 Output Terms; bfm-grace-off is true for redistributed MACE-OFF files), these bundled images make the flag true. Records that stay false (bfm-lambda, bfm-mimic-polymathic, bfm-aamfm) do NOT redistribute the third-party weights. I set noncommercial=true and spell out in status that generation needs neither oracle, so the curator can see exactly what the flag rests on and overrule it if they scope 'artifact' to the model's own files. The ported OpenFold3 weights claim checks out: openfold3/weights/of3_ported_weights.provenance.json (HTTP 200) states "license": "Apache-2.0", weight_family openfold3, with source and converted SHA-256. (d) ACCESS ROUTE MISSED: the proposal claims 'API: none'. Two public NVIDIA Spaces are linked from the official card and are live - nvidia/rfd4-proteina-zerogpu (stage RUNNING, zero-a10g) and nvidia/rfd4-proteina-space (stage RUNNING, rtx-pro-6000) - a hosted interactive route that screens inputs and designs with SecureDNA. Added to the corrected record. Gating: none anywhere (model, Diffusers mirror, dataset all gated=false).

identity.note: Attempt to refute failed. The bioRxiv API record (DOI 10.64898/2026.10.01.756017, v1, posted 2026-10-05) and the rendered landing page (HTTP 200 on re-fetch; title matches) name the same model as the repository google-deepmind/alphaprotein-novo (GitHub API: fork=false, created 2026-10-05, pushed 2026-10-06, description 'AlphaProtein Novo', license Apache-2.0), whose README cites that exact DOI in its BibTeX and whose author list (Wu, Abramson, Frerix, ... Hassabis, Arnold, Kohli, Wang) matches the preprint's. Corresponding institution on the preprint is Google DeepMind, so the repo is author-endorsed, not a third-party re-upload. Weights are served from a Google-controlled bucket (storage.googleapis.com/alphaprotein_novo) named in that README, not a mirror. No hub card exists, so no hub-identity check applies. Dedup: no 'alphaprotein'/'novo' collision in the identity baseline for this model; the nearest baseline records are distinct models (bfm-alphaproteo = AlphaProteo binder design, paper-only; bfm-rfdiffusion2 and bfm-rfdiffusion = RosettaCommons; bfm-alphafold-3 = AF3, which AP Novo only consumes as an optional refolding stage). Not a renamed version of any of them. One nitpick in the proposal's claims text: it says the proposal was 'absent from the baseline (no alphaprotein string in the identity TSV)' — correct, but note bfm-alphaproteo normalizes to 'alphaproteo', a near neighbour that must not be merged.

scope.note: Pretrained generative diffusion model, reusable, and used across design problems rather than one fixed task: the weights terms define the AP Novo Generator as 'the generative diffusion model for de novo protein structure and sequence generation', and the README exposes several conditioning regimes (full vs partial residue motif, indexed vs unindexed motif residues, novel scaffold vs partial diffusion from an existing structure) over user-supplied motifs and ligands, with three worked campaigns. That is the same class as the displayed RFdiffusion / RFdiffusion2 protein-design records, so including it does not widen catalog scope and does not invoke any structural-model exception (AP Novo is not a structure predictor; AF3/AF3-LA refolding is an optional downstream stage with its own separately licensed weights). Modality 'protein' is correct. Caveat recorded rather than used to reject: the released artifact is a design generator whose demonstrated application domain is enzyme design, so the record must not be described as a general protein representation model.

artifact.note: Weights exist as claimed and are reachable without any gate: HEAD on https://storage.googleapis.com/alphaprotein_novo/generator.bin.zst returns HTTP 200, content-type application/zstd, content-length 547140096 (547 MB), last-modified 2026-09-28. The repo has no tagged releases, so the weights are not release assets — the bucket object is the sole weights route; the proposal's wording already says this. terms.note: noncommercial=true is correct, but the proposed status wording understates two restrictions I read in the terms text, so corrections are required. Confirmed: code Apache-2.0 (GitHub license API spdx_id Apache-2.0; README 'Licensing & Disclaimer'); all other materials CC-BY 4.0; generator weights under the AlphaProtein Novo Generator Model Parameters Terms of Use (last modified 2026-10-05), available 'only ... for non-commercial use by, or on behalf of, non-commercial organizations' with commercial activities and research on behalf of commercial organizations excluded, plus an incorporated Prohibited Use Policy and separate Output Terms of Use; outputs may not be used to train, fine-tune or distill similar de novo design models; model parameters must not be published or shared outside the user's own organization. Also: Google 'may at any time suspend or terminate' access, and the terms contemplate being asked to verify name and organization when requesting access — no sign-in or form blocks the current download, but access is revocable, which the status should not hide behind 'no gate'. The displayed status must therefore mention the no-redistribution and output-training restrictions, since a reader choosing a model for a collaboration with industry or for distillation would otherwise be misled.

name: CONCH-Z
reason: Found in the MahmoodLab rename sweep: a new pathology vision-language model released 2026-10-12, not in the baseline. Paper, repository, gated weights and exact terms are all verified, but the family identity is unresolved: CONCH-Z keeps CONCH v1.5's frozen vision encoder and trains only a new text tower, so it is either a new record, an alias/variant of bfm-conch (which is CONCH v1, Nature 2024), or a thin derivative the catalog should reject. Not a duplicate of a baseline record: no 'prompteina' normalized name or alias in fm_identity.tsv. It IS derived from the displayed record bfm-proteina-complexa (NOTICE: 'Prompteina builds on NVIDIA Proteina-Complexa ... commit aa64cc0f89'), but it has its own preprint, corpus, text interface and two new checkpoints, so it is a distinct record, not a rename. Note for the curator: NOTICE gives the upstream repo as NVIDIA-Digital-Bio/Proteina-Complexa while the baseline bfm-proteina-complexa record cites NVIDIA-BioNeMo/Proteina-Complexa; that is a pre-existing baseline question, not a defect of this proposal, and was not resolved here.

scope.note: In scope. Pretrained, reusable artifact (two released inference checkpoints) with one natural-language conditioning interface spanning fold/topology, secondary structure, tertiary motifs, global shape, surface properties, interface properties and function, plus two design regimes (monomer generation, target binder design), so broader than one task and not a single-task predictor or a thin fine-tune: text-conditioned pretraining on a new paired corpus adds an input interface the parent model does not have. Consistent with the displayed Proteina / La-Proteina / Proteina-Complexa records. MODALITY CORRECTION: the same model was proposed independently in two lanes, protein.json (modality 'protein') and multimodal.json (modality 'multimodal'); these must collapse to ONE record. 'protein' is the correct routing: the catalog's modality axis is the biological data type, and here that is protein structure, as for bfm-proteina; natural language is a conditioning interface, not a second biological modality, and reading it as one would also reclassify any text- or label-conditioned model. The multimodal reading is defensible but is the weaker fit, and the duplicate is the harder defect.

artifact.note: Weights exist as claimed and are ungated. HF API api/models/jleechung/prompteina: gated false, private false, disabled false, createdAt 2026-10-09, lastModified 2026-10-13, usedStorage 7421095816 bytes, siblings = .gitattributes, README.md, SHA256SUMS, config.json, prompteina-binder.ckpt, prompteina-monomer.ckpt. Nothing downloaded. Two dependencies that make the artifact non-self-contained, both stated by the authors and both to be reflected in the record: (a) 'The autoencoder is not included with these weights' (HF card, Usage) - complexa_ae.ckpt comes from the code repo's env/download_startup.sh --complexa; (b) the frozen Qwen3-Embedding-8B and Qwen3-8B text encoders are not in the checkpoints and are fetched from the Hub at build time (HF card; repo README Installation, ~32 GB GPU memory). Also material and absent from both proposals: 'These checkpoints are for inference only and cannot resume training' (HF card), so reuse means conditional generation, not further pretraining. The GitHub repo has no releases (releases endpoint returns []), so the Hub is the only weight route. REFUTED CLAIM: the training corpus is NOT released. api/datasets/jleechung/prompteina-data: siblings = README.md only, usedStorage 0, and the card reads 'We are preparing the dataset for public release. It will be available shortly.' protein.json's claim of 'paired text-structure data and two checkpoints released' is wrong on the data half; multimodal.json states this correctly.

terms.note: Three-way split confirmed from the repository's own files, not inferred. Root LICENSE is a 118-byte pointer ('This repository contains multiple components covered by different licenses. See the licenses/ directory for details.'), which is why the GitHub licence endpoint reports SPDX NOASSERTION. NOTICE Licenses table: Code = Apache License 2.0; Model weights = NVIDIA Open Model License; Data assets = CC BY 4.0; Third-party code and docs = BSD 3-Clause / MIT / Apache 2.0; plus NVIDIA Trustworthy AI terms by reference. licenses/license_weights.txt is the NVIDIA Open Model License Agreement, preamble: 'Models are commercially usable. You are free to create and distribute Derivative Models.' licenses/license_datasets.txt is the CC BY 4.0 legal code. HF cardData: license other, license_name nvidia-open-model-license, gated false. noncommercial: false is correct - no NC term on any confirmed artifact or access route. Two precision corrections: (1) the CC BY 4.0 line covers the repository's data assets, NOT the unreleased Prompteina-Data corpus, whose terms are unstated; protein.json's status sentence 'paired text-structure training data CC BY 4.0' asserts terms for an artifact that does not exist yet. The HF repo is in the official `nvidia` org and the code repo in the official `RosettaCommons` org, so neither is a third-party re-upload. The project page carries the full author list, with affiliation 1 Institute for Protein Design and affiliation 4 NVIDIA Corporation, ending in David Baker, matching the README's 'Baker Lab x NVIDIA GenAIR' line. Not a duplicate of a baseline record: no catalog record contains the string 'RFD4' or any rfd4-proteina URL, and the normalized names rfdiffusion / rfdiffusion3 / rfd3 / proteina / laproteina / proteinacomplexa do not collide with rfd4proteina. It is a successor of both lines, but the baseline already keeps RFdiffusion, RFdiffusion2, Proteina, La-Proteina and Proteina-Complexa as separate records, so a separate record follows precedent rather than creating a rename collision. The lane's existing_record_updates entries for bfm-rfdiffusion and bfm-proteina correctly leave the alias-vs-separate-record call to the curator; nothing must be done twice.

scope.note: In scope. One pretrained, reusable matched pair (flow model + autoencoder, 435,622,465 stored parameters, FP32 EMA weights) serves many design tasks, not one: the README lists monomers, protein and DNA binders, antibodies and nanobodies, enzymes and motif scaffolding, and small-molecule pockets, and a PEFT LoRA adapter plus the pretrained base in base/ make fine-tuning an intended route. This is not a single-task predictor and not a thin fine-tune of someone else's checkpoint; the autoencoder is newly unified (147-class residue vocabulary, 32-dim latent) rather than inherited. Modality: 'protein' is defensible but it is the weaker of two readings and the lane said so. The release conditions on and generates nucleic acids, glycans and ligands (README gallery alt text names a nanobody complex, protein-DNA binder, RNA pseudoknot, ligand pocket, glycan complex and protein assembly), which in the baseline sends Proteina-Complexa and RoseTTAFold All-Atom / RF3 to 'complex'; the same baseline keeps RFdiffusion/RFD3 at 'protein' although RFD3 also handles ligand and nucleic-acid context. I keep 'protein' to follow the direct lineage record (bfm-rfdiffusion) and flag 'complex' as a legitimate curator override; this is a placement judgment, not a factual error.

identity.note: Paper, repo and hub artifact are the same model and author-endorsed. arXiv:2610.19592 (citation_arxiv_id meta, submitted 2026/10/14, v1 only, no withdrawal) is 'InstructPro2: Natural Language and Biological Grounding Guided De Novo Protein Design' by Novak, Song, Li, Xie, Li (CMU Ray and Stephanie Lane Computational Biology Dept / LTI; Lambda Inc). The paper body links exactly one code URL, github.com/chovak/InstructPro2; arXiv submission history reads 'From: Charles Novak', and the repo owner login is chovak. That paper-linked repo's README links the hub model (charlesnovak/InstructPro2) and dataset (charlesnovak/InstructPro2Bench), and both hub cards link back to the same arXiv ID and GitHub repo with the same five-author BibTeX, so the hub artifacts are endorsed through the official repo rather than third-party re-uploads. gh api users/chovak exposes no real name or company, so the GitHub-to-author link rests on the paper's own availability statement plus the arXiv submitter name, not on a profile field. No baseline collision: normalized 'instructpro2' is absent from fm_identity.tsv (486 displayed records). Nearest names are distinct models by other groups or earlier work: bfm-instructprotein (InstructProtein, HICAI-ZJU, ACL 2024, multimodal), bfm-instructbiomol, bfm-instructcell, bfm-mol-instructions, and bfm-pinal-denovo-pinal, which this paper uses as its strongest baseline ('We use the released T2struc-1.2B checkpoint and the authors' PinalDesign routine'). No earlier 'InstructPro' v1 record exists in the baseline, so this is not a renamed or versioned duplicate of a catalog entry.

scope.note: In scope and not a thin fine-tune. Pretrained generative artifact: 205.7M <function description, protein> pairs from UniProtKB (abstract and contribution bullet), with a text encoder plus frozen ChemBERTa (ligand) and esm2_t12_35M_UR50D (antigen) encoders feeding gated cross-attention adapters into a decoder initialized from ProGen2-large-BFD90; 'The full model contains 3.2B parameters' (Methods). Reusable beyond one task: three released checkpoints cover text-conditioned generation (full sequence or spans in a scaffold), ligand-binding design conditioned on SMILES, and antibody HCDR1-3 design conditioned on antigen chains, and the Stage 1 checkpoint is documented as the starting point for further finetuning (hub card checkpoint table; repo README 'The three models' table and train_stage2_* scripts). Not a single-task predictor and not a structural predictor. Modality 'protein' is correct by catalog precedent: output is always a protein sequence, matching bfm-pinal-denovo-pinal (text -> protein, modality protein). 'multimodal' would be defensible given text+SMILES+antigen conditioning, but the catalog reserves that for models whose outputs span modalities (InstructProtein, Evolla), so protein is the better fit.

identity.note: Paper, repository and hub artifact are the same, author-endorsed model. The preprint's Code availability section names https://github.com/GENTEL-lab/AlphaEnzyme; the Hugging Face card links back to that repository; the GitHub org is 'GENTEL lab' (Zheng lab, Global Institute of Future Technology, Shanghai Jiao Tong University), matching corresponding author Shuangjia Zheng (shuangjia.zheng@sjtu.edu.cn) in the bioRxiv record. No third-party re-upload involved. Not a duplicate or rename of a baseline record: fm_identity.tsv has no enzyme-function record under any AlphaEnzyme alias; the nearest same-lab records are bfm-eva (rna), bfm-la-ribo (rna) and bfm-aamfm (protein), all different models, and bfm-zymctrl is an unrelated generative enzyme LM. EnzymeCAGE (Liu et al., Nature Catalysis 9:148-160, 2026) is cited in the preprint as a prior baseline, not as the same model; I did not independently check the proposal's claim that EnzymeCAGE was previously rejected, since that register was outside my task. Minor: the proposed record writes the GitHub URL as GENTEL-Lab/AlphaEnzyme while the canonical owner spelling is GENTEL-lab (GitHub is case-insensitive, both resolve). Separate inconsistency, not an identity failure: the Hugging Face DATASET card points code to https://github.com/yliust/AlphaEnzyme/tree/liuyong, which returns 404 (gh api and web); yliust is GitHub user 'Yong Liu', the preprint's first author, so this is a stale author pointer, not a rival artifact.

scope.note: In scope. Methods 4.3: the shared representation was pretrained on a curated RHEA collection of 503,770 labelled enzyme-reaction pairs (478,356 train / 25,414 validation) before kinetic or mutational supervision, and three readouts (catalytic compatibility, log10 kcat and log10 Km, variant fitness) sit on one 1,152-dimensional shared encoder interface. That is broader than one task and is not a single-task predictor. Modality 'protein' is defensible for the enzyme lane; an argument exists for 'multimodal' because the second input is a reaction (SMILES/DRFP), but the catalogue's protein lane already holds enzyme-function models, so I did not force a change. Caveat recorded under artifact: the released weights are task-specific heads over a third-party structural trunk, so 'foundation model' follows the authors' own wording.

artifact.note: Weights exist as claimed and are ungated. Hugging Face API for GENTEL-Lab/AlphaEnzyme: gated=false, private=false, createdAt 2026-11-04T06:57:49Z, five .pt siblings (specificity/specificity_final.pt 53,191,760 B; kinetics seeds 1234/2026/3407 about 1.29 GB each; mutation_final.pt 562,680,074 B) plus SHA256SUMS listing a digest for each of the five. The task tables are a separate ungated dataset repo, GENTEL-Lab/AlphaEnzyme-data (gated=false, same creation timestamp), which the proposal describes but the proposed record does not link. Three limits the record should state: (1) the release does not bundle the upstream Protenix/ESM-C foundation weights, so the structural trunk must be obtained separately, and full inference on new sequences also needs P2Rank/Java and a CUDA GPU; (2) mutation_final.pt is a bundle of 328 component fits (13 stochastic components x 3 seeds + 2 ridge, over 8 folds, per configs/mutation.json), not a single network, and scoring requires submitting a whole candidate library and choosing a released fold; (3) the GitHub README's download commands reference AlphaEnzyme_checkpoints.zip and AlphaEnzyme_data.zip, which do not exist in the hub listing - the working route is the hub card's 'hf download GENTEL-Lab/AlphaEnzyme --local-dir .' plus the dataset repo. Nothing was downloaded. Verified by listing only.

terms.note: noncommercial=true is correct, but the wording needs tightening. The repository LICENSE is a short (2,097 byte) custom document: a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 acceptance paragraph followed by three Use Restrictions (no commercial use; no use in drug development or discovery, including target, hit or lead identification, candidate selection and lead optimization; no use of outputs to train other LLMs, protein-structure-prediction technology or similar third-party models). It does not reproduce the CC BY-NC 4.0 operative text and refers to terms 'as defined below' that the file does not define, so it is a custom non-commercial agreement citing CC BY-NC 4.0, not a CC licence. GitHub classifies it NOASSERTION. Neither hub repo carries any licence metadata: cardData for the model repo is only {tags:[enzyme, protein, pytorch, biology]} and the dataset card likewise has no licence field, so the hub artifacts are covered only by the repository LICENSE as asserted in the GitHub README ('AlphaEnzyme code, model weights and released data ... non-commercial research use'). Third-party runtimes keep their own terms (Protenix, OpenFold, TorchDrug Apache-2.0; P2Rank MIT; ESM/ESMC upstream terms). The preprint itself is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (bioRxiv API license field cc_by_nc_nd). One material fact the proposal omits: the competing-interests statement records that Bota Biosciences funded the study and 'holds exclusive commercialization rights to the models, code and results', with SJTU retaining research use - which is why the non-commercial and no-drug-discovery clauses should be read as hard constraints, not boilerplate.

urls.note: All five URLs in the proposed record were re-fetched by me and show what their labels claim: bioRxiv v1 landing page HTTP 200 with the matching title; bioRxiv details API HTTP 200 with DOI 10.64898/2026.11.04.764416, date 2026-11-05, version 1, license cc_by_nc_nd, category bioinformatics; GitHub repo HTTP 200 via gh api (created 2026-11-02T12:42:17Z, pushed 2026-11-02T12:44:32Z, licence NOASSERTION, 2 stars); raw LICENSE HTTP 200; Hugging Face model page HTTP 200 and its API HTTP 200. I additionally fetched the v1 full-text HTML and PDF (HTTP 200) and the dataset API/card (HTTP 200). No aggregator was used as evidence. Correction: the data artifact (https://huggingface.co/datasets/GENTEL-Lab/AlphaEnzyme-data) should be in code_links and sources, since the record's status sentence and description both refer to separately published task tables.

text.note: Numbers check out against the preprint: top-1 retrieval 30.1% vs 17.2% for EnzymeCAGE on the 279-query temporally held-out cohort; Km Spearman 0.640 at the Seq-40 threshold (0.656 at Seq-99); TrpB enrichment at a 16-variant budget without target-specific fitness training; year 2026. No invented identifiers. Two text corrections: (1) io misstates the interface - per Methods 4.1 the model takes an amino-acid sequence and a reaction as canonical or atom-mapped SMILES, and the structure-grounded representation is produced internally, not supplied by the user; (2) description and status should name the separate data repo and say that upstream Protenix/ESM-C weights are not included. Two honesty points the record could carry but does not: kcat is only competitive (0.391 at Seq-40, below EITLEM at 0.422), and the ProteinGym mutation evaluation is described by the authors themselves as exploratory because the eight proteins were examined during model development. Neither is an inflated claim in the record as written, since the description cites only Km and TrpB.

identity.note: The NAR 2025 paper (10.1093/nar/gkaf044, Li ... Bar-Joseph, Jager; Sanofi Digital R&D), the Sanofi-Public/mRNA-LM repository (not a fork, created 2024-09-10, last push 2026-10-28 dependency bump) and the Sanofi CDN archives are the same model, and the paper names this repository. The Zenodo record 14606043 is a snapshot of JasmineSizhen/mRNA-LM, which is the first author's GitHub fork of Sanofi-Public/mRNA-LM (gh api: fork=true, parent Sanofi-Public/mRNA-LM). It is author-made and cited in the paper's Data availability statement, so it is acceptable as a code archive, but it is not the canonical repository. Not a duplicate: the baseline holds bfm-codonbert (CDS-only, Genome Research 2024), bfm-utr-lm (a different group) and other mRNA records, none named mRNA-LM. Partial overlap: the CDS component is the same CodonBERT.zip that the CodonBERT repository links. The alias '3UTRBERT (Sanofi)' must stay qualified because a separate 3UTRBERT (Yang et al., Adv Sci 2024, cited as ref. 30 in this paper) exists and was surfaced in the same discovery sweep.

scope.note: In scope as rna. Released reusable pretrained artifacts are three self-supervised BERT component models (5UTRBERT, CodonBERT, 3UTRBERT); the paper describes over 10 million full-length mRNA sequences from multiple species. Correction needed: no pretrained joint/integrated checkpoint is released. The CLIP integration module is trained only during task fine-tuning (FullModel.py loads the three component checkpoints with from_pretrained from hard-coded /mount/data/models/ paths; paper Fig. 1 legend: 'Models are fine-tuned for specific prediction tasks using the CLIP methodology'). No fine-tuned task heads are released either. The record must not imply a downloadable integrated full-length model.

identity.note: Paper, Zenodo record and portal are one model, and the authors endorse all three. The bioRxiv preprint (10.64898/2026.10.12.758266, v1, posted 2026-10-18) cites Zenodo record 23201637, the ultrarnalab.com portal, Code Ocean capsule 2602506 and the web server in its Data/Code availability sections. The record has an earlier version (22125275, 2026-08-30) under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22125274. No baseline duplicate: nothing in fm_identity.tsv matches ribogram, ultrarnalab, 23201637 or 758266, and the nearest names (RIBOSPAN, La-Ribo, RibonanzaNet2) are different models.

scope.note: This is a self-supervised MLM encoder (12 layers, hidden size 1,280, 20 heads, parallel 1/3/5/7/9-nt convolutions plus RoPE attention), pretrained on about 40 million ncRNA sequences from RNAcentral 25.0, Rfam 15.0 and Ensembl 115. The release exposes an embedding and attention API plus several heads: ncRNA 13-category and 88-family classification, RNA-protein, RNA-RNA and RNA-chromatin interaction, and LoRA adaptation. So it is reusable and covers more than one task, and the modality 'rna' is correct.

artifact.note: Confirmed beyond the proposer's check. The Zenodo API lists the four archives and a HEAD request on '2. Model Availability.zip' returns 200 with no login. I range-read only the last 64 KB (the zip central directory, no weights downloaded), which lists RiboGRAM.pkl (3,389,985,992 bytes), PLM-CDS.pkl, PLM-mRNA.pkl, ribogram_ncrna13_head.pt, ribogram_ncrna88_head.pt and RiboGRAM-RPI/RPI_plus/RRI/RCI.pkl. The inner RiboGRAM.zip inside '1. Source Code.zip' also holds checkpoints/RiboGRAM.pkl, both heads, infer.py, the ribogram/ package and README.md, and has no LICENSE file. Caveat: by the Zenodo description, RiboGRAM-3D 'requires one additional STAR RNA language-model backbone checkpoint', 'not a RiboGRAM checkpoint and is not included in this release'. That conflicts with the paper's description of RiboGRAM-3D as built on the frozen RiboGRAM encoder. The released 3D package is therefore not runnable from this release alone. Code Ocean returned 403. The portal's own downloads are 'currently only open to reviewers' and the web server sits behind a login.

terms.note: The proposal is incomplete on terms. The Zenodo record metadata says license cc-by-4.0 and access_right open, and the preprint text is CC BY 4.0. However, the record's own description says: 'The supplied materials do not specify one project-level license. Software, model checkpoints, and datasets may be subject to different terms.' The code package has no LICENSE file, the portal footer reads 'All rights reserved', and the datasets bundle third-party resources (RNAcentral, Rfam, Ensembl, bpRNA, ArchiveII, DRfold2/PDB, ENCODE/eCLIP, RNA-Chrom) under their own terms. I found no non-commercial terms anywhere, so noncommercial=false stands, but that does not make the licence clean or permissive. The status must quote the disclaimer, not just say 'CC BY 4.0'. I did not hold for this because the formal Zenodo licence grant comes from the first author and no conflicting restrictive terms exist for code or weights; the issue is ambiguity, and the corrected status wording below records it.

urls.note: bioRxiv landing 200 (title matches); the JATS URL redirects (301) to /content/biorxiv/early/2026/10/18/2026.10.12.758266.source.xml (200); Zenodo API 200; the portal ribogram.php 200. https://zenodo.org/records/23201637 and the DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23201637 both end in 403 for this client, which is CERN bot blocking, so the landing page could not be checked here. It is still the URL the paper cites, and the API confirms the same record. The usage page redirects to login.php (login wall), and Code Ocean returns 403. No aggregator pages are used.

text.note: Three corrections. (a) The description says the model learns positional gradients 'across nine organisms'. In the paper, the nine-organism result comes from k-mer profiling of ncRNA vs coding sequences; pretraining used about 40 M ncRNAs from RNAcentral, Rfam and Ensembl. (b) The base-pair recovery gain is relative to the authors' own CDS- and mRNA-pretrained control models (PLM-CDS, PLM-mRNA). It is author-reported. (c) RiboGRAM-3D is described as 'released'/'ships', but the release omits the backbone it needs (an external STAR checkpoint), so io and status must say so. Year 2026 is correct.

text.note: Mostly factual. Corrections: (a) use_cases lists 'perturbation prediction' as a use case. The framework README advertises perturbation-prediction fine-tuning, but the v2 paper says perturbation-response benchmarks are 'important future directions' and urges caution on perturbation response. The evaluated downstream use is drug mechanism-of-action linear probing on Sci-Plex3 embeddings, so this is reworded. (b) The description implied that the Cell Ontology loss came from later fine-tuning. Per v2 Sec. 4.4, the hierarchical cross-entropy is part of multitask pretraining of the 2026 Llama checkpoints, while the 2025 BERT multitask checkpoints were fine-tuned with multi-label cell type/tissue classification and an adversarial donor loss. MLM+RDA variant added. (c) Status now mentions the vLLM-format copies. Year 2025 (v1) is correct. Preprint only, not peer reviewed.

identity.note: Same model across paper, repo and hub. Research Square preprint 10.21203/rs.3.rs-11012643/v1 (posted 2026-09-18; Nature Portfolio 'In Review'; Yu Zhong is 2nd author) states in its Code availability section that the official repository is github.com/yzhong36/spaGFM. The repo (owner Yu Zhong, Indiana University; MIT) has the identical title and abstract and its README links the Model Zoo at huggingface.co/tinywind123/spaGFM. The hub account's full name is 'Yu Zhong'. The hub repo is author-endorsed, not a third-party re-upload. The proposal's audit note says the preprint does not link the repository. That holds only for the Crossref metadata: the PDF full text does link the repo. No baseline match by name, alias, URL or DOI (searched fm_identity.tsv for spagfm, yzhong36, tinywind123 and rs-11012643; the catalog JSON/MD files also have no match). It is distinct from Nicheformer, Novae and scGPT-spatial, which the paper benchmarks as separate comparators.

scope.note: This is a pretrained, reusable spatial-transcriptomics foundation model: self-supervised on 43.9M cells from 132 human and mouse samples (Xenium, CosMx, MERSCOPE; 20 tissues). It outputs frozen cell-level and neighbourhood-level embeddings used zero-shot and fine-tuned across several tasks (cell-type/niche label transfer, TLS detection, perturbation-response prediction, glomerular organisation). Modality 'spatial' is consistent with the baseline ST records (Nicheformer, Novae, scGPT-spatial). One nuance is not a scope failure: spaGFM is not an expression encoder on its own. Its node features come from a frozen scGPT whole-human checkpoint, so the model sits on top of scGPT. The paper itself calls the case studies proof-of-concept and hypothesis-generating.

artifact.note: The HF API (tinywind123/spaGFM) shows gated=false and private=false, created 2026-06-17, last modified 2026-08-27. The repo contains inference, fine-tuning and pretraining code (stRoamer/training/train.py, run_train.py) and two tutorials that snapshot_download the hub repo. The paper also describes 3M and 15M variants, which are not released. There are no GitHub releases. Weights were not downloaded.

identity.note: arXiv 2306.11207 (Ikezogwo et al.), GitHub wisdomikezogwo/quilt1m (first author's account; LICENSE copyright lists the paper's authors) and hub repos wisdomik/QuiltNet-B-32/-B-16/-B-16-PMB are linked to each other: the README's checkpoint section links all three hub repos, and the hub cards link back to the repo and carry the tag arxiv:2306.11207. Author-endorsed, not a re-upload. Not a duplicate: the baseline has no quilt/QuiltNet name, alias or URL. Nearest records are CONCH (displayed), PLIP (held) and OmiCLIP/Loki, which are distinct models. Quilt-LLaVA (arXiv 2312.04746) is a separate follow-on model and is not covered by this record.

scope.note: Pretrained histopathology vision-language (CLIP) model, domain-adapted on about 1M image-text pairs. It is reusable for zero-shot classification, linear probing and cross-modal retrieval (13 patch-level datasets), so it is broader than one task. The same class as displayed CONCH; PLIP is held on terms only, not on scope. Modality spatial (pathology) is correct.

artifact.note: Hub API (2026-11-06): all three checkpoints are public and ungated (gated=false) and list open_clip_pytorch_model.bin plus config and tokenizer files; B-32 and B-16 also have pytorch_model.bin. B-32 additionally holds undocumented files (dino_checkpoint.pth.tar, cyto_histo.pth.tar, all_inclusive.pth.tar). The proposal omitted the third official checkpoint, QuiltNet-B-16-PMB (ViT-B/16 with a PubMedBERT text encoder), which the README links and which I verified. Nothing downloaded.

terms.note: Code: MIT, from the GitHub licence API (spdx MIT) and the LICENSE file. The README's License section covers both code and pretrained model. Weights: all three hub cards declare license: mit and are ungated. The cards also carry the clause inherited from the OpenAI CLIP card that puts any deployed use, commercial or not, out of scope. Data: Quilt-1M access requires agreeing to terms 'committing to its specified research use'. The Zenodo record 8239942 has access_right 'restricted' and no licence field. noncommercial=true is correct under the any-artifact rule, but the basis is the research-use data terms (plus the card's use clause), not the PLIP precedent: PLIP lacks a weight licence, whereas QuiltNet weights are MIT. Status wording is accurate.

urls.note: All proposed URLs fetched with HTTP 200: arXiv abs, DataCite DOI, GitHub repo, both hub pages. Corrected record adds the B-16-PMB hub page (200). The paper link was labelled 'arXiv (NeurIPS 2023)', but the arXiv page itself shows no venue or comments. NeurIPS 2023 (oral) is stated only in the authors' README; I did not check proceedings (a DBLP query returned no parseable result). Label changed to 'arXiv', and the venue is attributed to the README in the audit note.

text.note: Description said the model was 'released as ViT-B/32 and ViT-B/16 checkpoints'. That is incomplete: there are three official checkpoints, one with a PubMedBERT text encoder. The paper states QuiltNet was trained by 'finetuning an OpenAI pre-trained CLIP model' with GPT-2/77 and PubMedBERT text encoders. Description and aliases corrected. I reworded the use case 'initialisation for pathology VLM fine-tuning' to the card's 'image task fine-tuning', because no specific downstream VLM initialisation was verified. io and year (2023) are correct. 'largely curated from YouTube' is supported: 802,148 of about 1M pairs.

name: ALHENA
reason: H&E encoder adapted from paired H&E and Xenium spatial transcriptomics (bioRxiv v1 25 Oct 2026; main window), well documented with BSD-3 package code and CC BY-NC 4.0 weights. But the released weights are rank-64 LoRA adapters (9.4M parameters) plus projection heads applied to MahmoodLab UNI2-h, which users must obtain separately under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. October rejected LoRA adapter releases on existing encoders (SPECTRA) as thin derivatives; ALHENA adds transcriptome-distilled cell space and reference atlases, so scope is a curator call, and releasing adapters for a no-derivatives base model is an unresolved terms question.

The hub card cites the same preprint, and the GitHub repo yyou1996/CIFM (owner name 'Yuning You', first author) links the hub as CIFM-100M. ynyou has only this one model on the hub. Not in the baseline: no normalized-name, alias (CI-FM) or URL match; the only baseline row is the October lead row. Correction: the 2026 preprint (10.64898/2026.08.12.743536) describes a retrained or extended CIFM, not demonstrably the hub checkpoint. Its corpus differs: 18,000 genes, 56 samples / 16 tissue types, agent-curated corpus. The 2025 paper reports ~100 slides and 32,000 genes. The 2026 paper also contradicts itself: it says the simulations use 'the 100-million-parameter configuration', yet 'we selected a 1B-parameter model as the operating point'. Code is available only on request. The proposed description, which says the 2026 preprint 'uses it' (the hub checkpoint), overstates this link.

scope.note: Self-supervised (masked-transcriptome) geometric GNN pretrained on ~23M cells from 10x Visium/Visium HD/Xenium V1/Xenium Prime. The released model exposes general functions: embed(adata), predict_cells_at_locations(adata, locations), and gene-channel matching (checked in models_cifm/cifm.py). Downstream uses include expression inference, linear-probe classification of sample conditions and perturbation simulation, so it is broader than one task. Modality 'spatial' matches how the baseline routes spatial-transcriptomics FMs (Nicheformer, scGPT-spatial, Novae).

artifact.note: HF API ynyou/CIFM: gated=false, private=false. Tree lists model.safetensors 568,752,944 bytes (LFS), and safetensors metadata gives 142,185,472 F32 parameters. identity.note: Paper, repository and hub artifacts are the same model from the same team. bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.10.26.760299 v1 (2026-10-28, corresponding author Woo Youn Kim, KAIST/HITS) has a Code availability statement naming github.com/kaist-ai-bio/kfold. The repo is owned by the KAIST AI-Bio GitHub organisation (blog www.kaist.ac.kr), is not a fork, and its README links the same DOI. The README author list matches the bioRxiv list. HF kaist-ai-bio/kfold and kfold-assets belong to the same org and the code downloads them by these IDs (runner.py ASSETS_REPO_ID; predict.py repo list). In the baseline, K-Fold appears only as a lead (no displayed or held record). It is distinct from the displayed AtlasFold/AtlasLM record (bfm-atlasfold), which it uses as a dependency. Hugging Face 'kfold'/'k-fold' search turned up only unrelated cross-validation fine-tunes, so there is no biology name collision. Minor: the kfold-assets card links github.com/SeonghwanSeo/kfold, which the GitHub API did not resolve; the official repo is the kaist-ai-bio one.

scope.note: Pretrained, reusable, MSA-free all-atom co-folding model. Inputs are protein, DNA, RNA and ligand entries (residue modifications allowed); the paper says it generalizes induced-fit prediction 'to arbitrary assemblies of proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecules'. It is evaluated across FoldBench interface types (P-P, P-L, P-NA, P-peptide) and on PXM-2025, MGBench, KinaseBench and GPCRBench, and it supports multi-state sampling from monomer ensembles without retraining. This is the same class as displayed complex records (AlphaFold 3, Chai-1, Protenix, BioKinema, AtlasFold), so it is not a single-task structural predictor. Modality 'complex' is correct. It is not a duplicate: normalized 'zatom2' matches only the lead row in fm_identity.tsv. Zatom-1 (arXiv 2602.22251, repo Zatom-AI/zatom) is a distinct predecessor with a different architecture, data and repo. The paper benchmarks 'Zatom-1 (released)' as a separate model. Zatom-2 is not in records_under_review.json, so no reserved ID has to be preserved. Cross-record follow-up: the bfm-zatom-1 audit_note says 'Successor Zatom-2 (October 2026) is held for missing artifacts', which becomes stale once Zatom-2 is added and should be updated in the same migration.

scope.note: The model is pretrained (about 5M OMol25 + OMat24 structures; data.md gives 3,986,754 + 1,009,850), reusable (public checkpoints, CLI, finetuning recipes) and multitask: generation, structure prediction, energy/force prediction, force-conditioned sampling, and transfer to protein backbones. It is broader than one task. The 'molecule' modality matches the displayed Zatom-1 precedent. The biology link runs through OMol25 (which includes biomolecular fragments and drug-like molecules) and the SCOPe protein-domain transfer. Scope therefore rests on the same, already-accepted reasoning as Zatom-1; it is not widened.

terms.note: Code: root LICENSE.md is the LBNL BSD-style 'Nucleus' licence (GitHub SPDX NOASSERTION; 3-clause BSD plus an Enhancements grant-back clause). models/zatom2/LICENSE.md is the same style under the 'Zatom-2' copyright, and the PyPI license fields of zatom-nucleus and zatom2 carry the same text. Weights: MIT appears only in the HF card YAML (license: mit, tag license:mit). The HF repo has no LICENSE file. Ungated. Data: the paper's Table 4 and docs/data.md give OMol25 and OMat24 as CC BY 4.0. However, the upstream facebook/OMol25 hub card is gated (gated='manual', card licence 'other'), and data.md says 'Accept the upstream dataset terms where required'. Retraining therefore needs approved access to Meta's gated OMol25 card. That access step was missing from the proposed status. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES: external UMA, ESMFold2, AFD/CT, Boltz, LeMat, CHGNet, ORB and MACE weights and tools keep their upstream terms, and some are gated. These are evaluation tools, not the Zatom-2 artifact. No non-commercial term was found on any Zatom-2 code, weight or release artifact, so noncommercial=false holds. That flag is not proof that the weights are cleanly licensed, because the only weight licence is card metadata. No hosted API was found.

urls.note: All four record URLs were fetched: arxiv.org/abs/2610.11454 200; github.com/Zatom-AI/nucleus 200 via the API and README; huggingface.co/Zatom-AI/Zatom-2 200 (page, raw README and API); pypi.org/project/zatom-nucleus/ 200 (page and JSON). Each shows what its label says. PyPI zatom-nucleus is the shared-infrastructure package ('Shared utilities and training infrastructure...'); the model package is zatom2 (pypi.org/pypi/zatom2/json 200). The label is sharpened to name the package. Minor: the zatom-nucleus PyPI Homepage metadata points to zatomai.github.io/nucleus (no hyphen); that URL is not used in the record. The project page zatom-ai.github.io/nucleus/ returns 200 and is not needed in the record.

text.note: The description, io and use_cases are mostly accurate, with three gaps and one overreach. (a) io omits the structure-prediction route, which the paper describes for OMat24 as conditioning on atom types and predicting geometry and lattice: atom types -> 3D geometry, plus the lattice for crystals. (b) Model sizes from paper Table 6 (S/base/L about 70M/140M/270M) add useful precision. (c) Energy/force prediction is an auxiliary pretraining task. Limitations G.2 says the authors 'do not intend to match specialized MLIPs' performance', so use_cases and the audit note should not present it as an MLIP replacement. (d) Status wording needs the training-data access route: OMol25 is behind Meta's manually gated card. Year 2026 is correct. The protein result (designability 67.8% to 74.8% after finetuning on 2,000 SCOPe domains) is a single low-data length-extrapolation experiment. The record's wording 'low-data protein backbone generation via transfer learning' is acceptable and not inflated.

scope.note: Pretrained reusable artifact: one released checkpoint (atomweaver.pt) plus bundled reference libraries and read-out heads, reusable on arbitrary user PDBs and extendable to new residue vocabularies by refitting only the small CPU read-out head. Residual scope risk, stated plainly: this is fixed-backbone inverse folding / sequence design, which is a narrow task family, and the catalog's own rule is 'broader than one task'. It is admissible only on the precedent already displayed in the baseline - bfm-proteinmpnn, bfm-ligandmpnn, bfm-esm-if1 are displayed 'protein' records of the same kind - and it is not a structure predictor, so the withheld structural-model exception is not being invoked. Modality 'protein' matches the precedent records (LigandMPNN also conditions on a non-protein/ligand context yet is stored as 'protein'); 'complex' is defensible but would break consistency with those rows. Verdict therefore does not reject on scope, but a reviewer who narrows the inverse-folding precedent should hold this record together with ProteinMPNN/LigandMPNN, not alone.

artifact.note: October blocker genuinely resolved. gh api repos/ProteinQure/atomweaver/releases returns exactly one release, tag v1.0.0, name 'Initial release', published_at 2026-10-16T15:57:34Z, draft=false, prerelease=false, with assets atomweaver.pt (201,811,099 bytes) and readout_train_clouds.npz (39,343,862 bytes); repos/.../tags lists v1.0.0. Repo contents listing shows LICENSE-CODE, LICENSE-WEIGHTS, README.md, atomweaver/, data/, examples/, scripts/, tests/. 201,811,099 bytes = 192.5 MiB, so the record's '~192 MB' is accurate.

terms.note: Code: LICENSE-CODE begins 'GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 19 November 2007'; GitHub licence endpoint reports spdx AGPL-3.0 at path LICENSE-CODE. Weights: LICENSE-WEIGHTS begins 'Attribution 4.0 International' (CC BY 4.0) and the README states weights are free to use including commercially, with attribution. Preprint is cc_by per the bioRxiv API and Crossref (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). No gating, no account, no click-through; no separate API/server. Bundled data (reference libraries, read-out heads, phi/psi table) and the readout_train_clouds.npz release asset carry no separate licence file - they are covered by the repo/weights terms as published, which is worth wording as 'bundled data under the repository terms' rather than asserting a distinct data licence. noncommercial=false is correct: AGPL-3.0 is copyleft, not non-commercial, and CC BY 4.0 permits commercial use. The AGPL network-copyleft caveat is already in the audit_note and should stay.

urls.note: All URLs in the proposed record fetched by me in this task: github.com/ProteinQure/atomweaver HTTP 200 (and via gh api); github.com/ProteinQure/atomweaver/releases/tag/v1.0.0 HTTP 200; www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.23.753608v1 HTTP 200 (reachability only - headers, no body read; the title/date/licence claims rest on the bioRxiv details API and Crossref for the same DOI, both fetched here). No aggregator is cited as evidence. One cosmetic repo defect, not a catalog error: the README's code-licence link points to 'LICENSE', while the file in the repo is LICENSE-CODE.

text.note: Three text fixes, all narrowing claims rather than widening them. (1) 'without retraining' is slightly too strong: the README requires a refitted read-out head (and reference rotamers in the fitting library) for a residue outside the shipped set - the model weights are not retrained, the small CPU head is refit in seconds. (2) description/status/use_cases mention only the 300-residue library, but the repo ships three vocabularies (canon20 = 20 classes, full300 = 300, exp450 = 450 with its own expanded library) and the README warns exp450 is not a superset of full300, so the two disagree on many positions - a user-visible caveat the record should carry. (3) io is accurate as far as it goes (designs.fasta, designs.csv with per-position top-3 probabilities, cloud PDBs) and gains from naming preds.json full distributions. No inflated performance claim is present in the record; the preprint's comparative results are not asserted in it, which is correct. year 2026 matches the preprint date and the release date.

The repository's own documentation also states that the root 'lm-pretrained' checkpoint is byte-identical to a ribozyme reinforcement-learning policy, so the identity of the pretrained artifact needs care.
